messages.body_plain:
Ola Raylson,

Obrigado por perguntar. FIELDimageR usa o pacote "raster" para ler imagens e teoricamente todas as imagens formato tif, jpg, e pdf são lidas com facilidade. Os sensores NIR que trabalhei geralmente retornam imagens em jpg ou tif, então voce pode usar o o código disponível no link https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P1 (Trocar tif do código para JPG, que e o formato da sua imagem).

Em seguida voce calcula os indices: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6
Faz o shape file: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P5
E extrai os valores: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P9

Apenas lembrando que o pacote não reconhece barcodes.

Tudo de bom,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: fieldIndex: Threshold to differentiate only not health plants
messages.subject_clean: fieldIndex: Threshold to differentiate only not health plants
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alexandre,

I don't know a specific index for differentiating browning plants from the soil. However, as a suggestion you can use a mask from when the plants were green to remove the soil. In other words, if you toke a picture before the disease causes changes on colors, you can make a mask and apply this mask on the mosaic with the disease. In this case geographic corrections (e.g. with GPC) are important to make the overlays of mosaics. Here is an example how to do it (EX3.RemSoil on "Removing soil"): https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P13

Another suggestion is to make a mask using a thermal camera and apply this mask on the RGB mosaic. You can easily differentiate plants (healthy or not) from the soil.

Another possibility is to use the function fieldMask more than once. For example, you first remove the green plants. Then you can use the output "newMosaic" to find other index to differentiate the browning/yellowish plants from the soil. As a suggestion, to calculate area (fieldArea, fieldCount, or fieldObject) you can use "is.na <http://is.na>(mask)<-1".

Let me know if this helps you or if you have more questions.
All the best,
Filipe

Thank you for asking.

About the first question I am not sure why the function is taking so long for you. You can try reducing the mosaic size/resolution with the function aggregate(). This is only to figure out if it is something related with the mosaic or with the function. 1.

The code does not reduce image resolution. Only if you are using the function
“aggregate()” from the “raster” package. Maybe you are seeing pixels around the
plants (mix of green and brown) that the mask didn’t remove (In this case, you
need to change the index to remove the soil). Could you share your image before
and after removing the soil step?

I have only RGB image, and I am trying to find out indices, please clarify,
whether these indices based on reflectance value or pixel value of each band.

A:
The function uses the relative value from pixels in the image. The user should
make the transformation from a digital number to a reflectance number. You need to

setwd("D://Flights_2019//G2F//25m//072619_25m")

                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape,

EX1.Info$fieldShape@data

write.csv(EX1.Info$fieldShape@data,
          "D://Flights_2019//G2F//25m//072619_25m//IHOT_VIs_072619.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

hist(EX1.Info$fieldShape$NGRDI)
